headline: Heterogeneous-model and raw-read phylogenetics tools advance evolutionary inference
label: Phylogenomic Inference Tools
summary: Mixture models fit heterogeneous phylogenomic data best, and new software now spans raw reads, protein structure, and gene concordance.
synthesis: The dominant thread is methodological infrastructure for phylogenetic inference, mostly addressing how evolutionary models and software handle heterogeneity. A large MBE simulation study reports that across-site mixture models, especially CAT-GTR, fit heterogeneous phylogenomic data best while maintaining accuracy on homogeneous data. IQ-TREE 3 adds mixture models, gene and site concordance factors, and divergence time integration to an open-source maximum-likelihood release. evo3D extracts structure-informed MSA subsets via fixed-count and fixed-distance 3D windows. Omni2Tree builds viral phylogenies directly from raw reads without assembly. The GBE horizontal gene transfer study is distinct, modeling transfer as a stochastic process over bacterial genera and linking match-length power-law exponents to direct versus indirect transfer networks. What is new is the breadth of tools operating on heterogeneous, structural, and raw-read inputs.
